content.value_statement: Creating plugin skills can be inconsistent without a clear structure. This skill gives practical guidance for planning, writing, organizing, and validating skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains required SKILL.md frontmatter and markdown structure.
Guides plugin skill directory planning for references, examples, and scripts.
Provides trigger phrase, writing style, and progressive disclosure guidance.
Includes a validation checklist for skill quality and resource references.
Points to the included original skill creator reference for broader methodology.
limitations: Does not include executable validation scripts.
Focuses on Claude Code plugin skills, not generic marketplace packaging.
Requires users to supply domain examples, assets, or private documentation.
Does not verify generated skills unless the agent runs separate tests.

use_cases.title: Create a Plugin Skill
use_cases.description: Plan the purpose, triggers, folder structure, and reusable resources for a new Claude Code plugin skill.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Refine trigger descriptions, split large instructions into references, and align writing style with skill guidance.

use_cases.title: Review Skill Organization
use_cases.description: Check whether instructions, references, examples, and scripts are placed in the right parts of a plugin skill.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code plugin skill for [domain]. Ask for missing trigger phrases before drafting the skill content.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Skill Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these user examples and recommend which guidance belongs in the main skill, references, examples, or scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Triggers and Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this SKILL.md for specific triggers, third-person frontmatter, imperative wording, and clear resource references.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Complex Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a complete plugin skill for [workflow], including reusable resources, validation steps, and progressive disclosure boundaries.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for internal API support.
output: A focused skill purpose and trigger list.
A plan for reference material, examples, and optional scripts.
A validation checklist for description quality and structure.

output_examples.output: Findings cover vague triggers, oversized main instructions, missing resource links, and writing style issues. Suggested edits are grouped by priority.

output_examples.input: Plan resources for a complex workflow skill.
output: Core workflow guidance stays in the main skill file.
Reusable examples and helper scripts are listed separately.

best_practices: Start from concrete user examples before writing skill instructions.
Keep the main skill file focused and move detailed material into references.
Validate trigger phrases, writing style, resource links, and examples before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague descriptions that fail to match real user requests.
Do not place every detailed reference in the main skill file.
Do not leave scripts, examples, or references unmentioned in the main instructions.

faq.question: Is this skill only for Claude Code plugins?
faq.answer: It focuses on Claude Code plugin skills, but many structure and writing principles apply to other skill formats.

faq.question: Can Codex use this guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can use it to author or review Claude Code compatible skills and marketplace content.

faq.question: Does it create files automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and workflows. File creation depends on the user request and the active coding agent.

faq.question: When should references be used?
faq.answer: Use references for detailed patterns, long documentation, migration notes, and material loaded only when needed.

faq.question: Does it perform a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It includes quality validation guidance, but a separate security review is still required.

faq.question: How should a new skill be tested?
faq.answer: Test expected trigger requests, verify resource links, inspect writing style, and confirm examples or scripts work.
